package_info.package_versions: latest/highest semver published to public registry
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are intentionally crafted to exploit the lack of enforced namespacing in public repositories. By registering package names that match internal/private dependencies used by target organizations, attackers can trick build systems into installing malicious code from the public registry instead of the intended internal package, enabling supply chain compromise.

execution_context.trigger: install-time (npm install, pip install, gem install)
execution_context.file_location: package.json (npm), setup.py (PyPI), gemspec (RubyGems), or main entrypoint

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Exfiltrates environment variables and potentially other sensitive data from the build or CI environment to an attacker-controlled server during package installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes automatically upon installation, sending environment data to an external server, which is not expected for a legitimate package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not exfiltrate environment variables or execute network requests during install-time. Legitimate postinstall scripts are rare and should not transmit sensitive data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use postinstall scripts for setup or telemetry, but never for exfiltrating secrets.
key_indicators: Presence of postinstall or install scripts making network requests
Access to environment variables or filesystem during install

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies internal package names used by target organizations (via log analysis, bug reports, or open source code).
Attacker registers public packages with the same names as internal dependencies, using a higher version number.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious package is available in public registry

attack_chain.action: Target organization's build or CI system resolves dependency to the public (malicious) package due to version precedence or misconfiguration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is installed in target environment

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at install-time, exfiltrating environment variables and secrets to attacker infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data (e.g., credentials, tokens, internal endpoints)

behavioral_signatures: Install-time scripts making outbound network requests
Access to environment variables or sensitive files during install
Unexpected postinstall or install hooks in packages with names matching internal dependencies
file_indicators: setup.py or gemspec files containing network exfiltration code
Presence of install scripts in packages with names matching internal/private dependencies
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to unknown or attacker-controlled domains during package installation
POST requests containing environment variable data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for install-time scripts in dependencies, especially those matching internal package names. Flag packages that make network requests or access environment variables during installation. Use allow-lists for internal dependencies and block installation of similarly named packages from public registries. Monitor build logs for unexpected install-time network activity.
